question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2}$ of two bolts is drawn from a population. The population has bolts of two different lengths, $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{8}\,\text{cm},$ distributed in the ratio $2:1.$ Calculate $\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}].$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sequence of random variables representing a random sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with population mean $\mu .$ Then, the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is given by

$$
\overset{―}{X}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{X}_{i}.
$$

Since $\overset{―}{X}$ is an unbiased estimator of $\mu ,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu .
$$

We're told that the bolts in the population have lengths $5\,\text{cm}$ and $\text{8}\,\text{cm},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $2:1.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean, we can consider a population consisting of $2+1=3$ bolts only with the following lengths:

$$
5\,\text{cm},\,5\,\text{cm},\,8\,\text{cm}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{3}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(2\cdot 5+8) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(10+8) \\  & =\frac{18}{3}. \\  & =6\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu =6\,\text{cm}.
$$
